title: Our Lady of Fatima (13 May)
hook: three shepherd children in Portugal in 1917, asking for prayer and penance

segments.voice: Yesterday, Good Shepherd Sunday and vocation, a call that starts with a name. Your line was he calls by name.

May 1917. Europe is at war, and Portugal has sent its own soldiers to the trenches. In the hills near a village called Fatima, three children are watching sheep: Lucia, ten, and her younger cousins Francisco and Jacinta, eight and seven. Around noon on the thirteenth, they later said, a flash like lightning came, and then a lady brighter than the sun, standing over a small oak tree. She asked them to come back on the thirteenth of every month, and to pray the rosary every day, for peace in the world and the end of the war.
screen: `MAY 1917: EUROPE AT WAR.` → `THREE CHILDREN WITH SHEEP.` → `PRAY THE ROSARY FOR PEACE.`

segments.voice: The children kept coming back, month after month through October. In August the local administrator held them, and that meeting came days late, away from the usual spot. The crowds grew from a handful of neighbors to thousands. On the thirteenth of October, in pouring rain, a huge crowd gathered, and witnesses, a reporter among them, described the sun seeming to spin and plunge. People still argue over what they saw. The message the children carried was simple and demanding: pray, especially the rosary; do penance; make sacrifices for sinners; pray for peace. Francisco and Jacinta took it so seriously that they offered up small hungers and discomforts, the way children would. Both died young, in the flu epidemic that followed the war, in 1919 and 1920. In 2017, a hundred years after the first appearance, Pope Francis canonized them at Fatima, two children named saints not for dying as martyrs but for how they lived. Lucia became a nun and lived until 2005. The Church judged the Fatima appearances worthy of belief in 1930, and popes have gone there on pilgrimage. But Catholic teaching calls these private revelations. They add nothing to the faith; the Church allows and encourages devotion to them, and does not require any Catholic to believe them. What Fatima asks for, though, is old: the rosary, and Mary as the one who points to her son. As she said in Luke, in the Douay-Rheims: "all generations shall call me blessed." On the thirteenth of May, some Catholics pray a decade for peace.
screen: `EVERY THIRTEENTH THROUGH OCTOBER.` · `PRAY, DO PENANCE, PRAY FOR PEACE.` · `TWO CHILDREN, SAINTS IN 2017.` · `WORTHY OF BELIEF, NOT REQUIRED.` · then, large: `ALL GENERATIONS SHALL CALL ME BLESSED.`

segments.voice: A decade of the rosary is one Our Father, ten Hail Marys and one Glory Be; if you pray, you can pray one now, on beads or on your fingers, for one place at war, naming the place first. If you don't pray, sit with the name of that place, and the children there, for ten slow breaths, and then a few more.
Fatima. The Portuguese village where three shepherd children said Mary appeared in 1917, asking for the rosary, penance and prayers for peace. Her day is the thirteenth of May. Today's word.
Your line: pray for peace. Ten Hail Marys, one place, one name. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: On 13 May Catholics often pray the rosary for peace, and pilgrims gather at the shrine in Fatima, Portugal, for candlelight processions; the appearances are approved as worthy of belief, but Catholics are not required to believe in them.

chat.says: Do Catholics have to believe Mary really appeared at Fatima?
options: No. The Church judged it worthy of belief, but it's private revelation, not required.
Yes; since 1930 it has been part of the faith every Catholic must accept.
No; the Church officially ruled that the visions were the children's imagination.
chat.meaning: Catholic teaching calls Fatima a private revelation: judged worthy of belief in 1930 and encouraged, but adding nothing to the faith and required of no one.

notes: Ages in May 1917: Lucia 10, Francisco 8 (born 11 June 1908), Jacinta 7 (born 11 March 1910). Confirm.
Crowd on 13 October 1917: often estimated at 30,000–70,000; script says 'a huge crowd'.
Portugal entered WWI in 1916 and sent troops to France in 1917; confirm 'has sent its own soldiers to the trenches' timing for May 1917.
Francisco died 4 April 1919, Jacinta 20 February 1920; canonized 13 May 2017. 'Among the youngest non-martyr saints' is a common description; confirm.
